statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System (公司名稱及所營事業預查線上申請系統, https://gcis.nat.gov.tw)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in Traditional Chinese script. An English name may be adopted only as an auxiliary registered name and must be recorded in the articles of association; the English name must be a direct Roman-alphabet transliteration or standard translation of the Chinese name and shall not contain terms likely to mislead as to government affiliation. Foreign-language names must be transliterated into Chinese in accordance with the MOEA-approved conversion table, and the chosen characters must not imply public authority.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Taiwan (臺灣) where used internally to imply official status
China (中國) where used to imply agency of the central government
International (國際) without evidence of cross-border scope
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name pre-review is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal (申訴) with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within 30 days of receipt of the rejection letter, setting out the grounds why the name is distinctive and not prohibited. If the original rejection is upheld, the applicant may bring an administrative lawsuit before the Taipei High Administrative Court within 2 months. An alternative fast-track remedy is to modify the proposed name and submit a new pre-review application online within 1-2 business days; the statutory pre-review fee is NT$300.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only with a registered physical service address and a licensed resident agent or representative in Taiwan; a pure virtual mailbox without a live administrative office may be rejected by the bank account opening unit and customs registration, particularly for bulk dehydrated spices export where trade-based money-laundering controls require demonstrable commercial substance. A serviced office with administrative staffing is acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 15% likelihood of unannounced MOEA, tax, or customs inspection during the first two operating years; probability increases to 35% if the registered office is found to be a virtual desk without records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 revision, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 23-47 and 57-64; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (effective 1 January 2020), Articles 9-12 and 30-31; Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Investment by Taiwan Compatriots (2016 amendment), Article 2, applied by reference to foreign investment.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR local bureau at the registered domicile), acting through the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform for enterprise registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company (Foreign-Invested Enterprise Company Registration Application Form).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum registered capital applies for a Wholly Foreign-Owned Limited Liability Company in this ordinary wholesale sector. Under the new Company Law, the sole shareholder must pay all subscribed capital in full within five years from the date of establishment, or within a shorter period prescribed by the Articles of Association. Cash contributions from Taiwan must be remitted through approved cross-strait banking channels, deposited into a dedicated capital contribution account in the company's name in mainland China, and verified by a certified public accountant; foreign-exchange registration with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange is required before capital is released.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED by the sole shareholder of [Company Name] that: 1. The company is established as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company with a registered capital of CNY [amount], subscribed entirely by the founding Taiwan shareholder. 2. The registered office is [Address], China, and the lease/use certificate is approved. 3. The capital contribution is remitted from Taiwan through permitted banking channels into a dedicated capital contribution bank account in mainland China and verified by a CPA before registration. 4. [Name] is appointed executive director and legal representative; [Name] is appointed supervisor; [Name] is appointed manager. 5. The appointed officers are authorized to execute all filings and apply for business, tax, customs, food and environmental registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan notary offices, Straits Exchange Foundation / Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits verification channel, and the local Administration for Market Regulation online name pre-registration service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain notarization of the Taiwan investor's corporate existence, current registered status, and signatory authorization. Forward the notarized document through the SEF/ARATS cross-strait authentication channel to the mainland notary association for verification. Simultaneously submit the proposed Chinese company name, business scope, and capital structure for pre-approval through the local Administration for Market Regulation online system.
required_dossiers: Notarized and authenticated Taiwan investor identification or company registration extract
Power of attorney for the authorized representative
Planned registered address evidence or lease intent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name application is queried due to identical or misleading similarity, resubmit up to three alternative names within five working days. If the Taiwan notarized document is challenged, request re-authentication through the SEF/ARATS channel before continuing with the formation application.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan jurisdiction: Ministry of Finance, Republic of China (Taiwan), administered through the National Taxation Bureau with jurisdiction over the place of business; tax services are available through the Ministry of Finance eTax portal. The payload identifies China as the sovereign country but Taiwan as the jurisdiction and a China WFOE as the entity. These identifiers do not establish one coherent tax jurisdiction: a mainland China WFOE is not, solely by that status, a Taiwan-registered taxpayer.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Taiwan-established company, complete company establishment and obtain the company registration documents, then apply to the competent National Taxation Bureau for tax registration and a business administration number before commencing business. A foreign company establishing a Taiwan branch must first complete branch registration with the competent authority and then register for tax. A foreign entity without a Taiwan establishment may have Taiwan tax registration obligations depending on its Taiwan activities and applicable rules; it should confirm the required registration route with the competent bureau. Mainland China WFOE registration in China does not itself procure a Taiwan tax ID or VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election for choosing pass-through or entity-level classification. Taiwan companies are generally taxed as separate entities; branches and other establishments are treated under the rules applicable to their legal form. No general hybrid-mismatch election changes this classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (VAT-type business tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover threshold exempts an ordinary company conducting taxable business from business registration and tax registration. The NTD 600,000 annual sales threshold commonly referenced for certain foreign electronic service suppliers is not a general threshold for this goods-trading activity. Confirm registration obligations against the taxpayer's actual Taiwan presence and activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan uses Government Uniform Invoices, including electronic invoices for taxpayers subject to the applicable e-invoice rules. Invoice issuance, transmission, and reporting are governed by Ministry of Finance requirements and applicable taxpayer/category rules. Taiwan does not impose a universal real-time pre-clearance or digital-stamping regime equivalent to systems that require tax-authority clearance before every invoice is issued.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Qualifying exports of goods may be zero-rated if the statutory export conditions are met and the taxpayer retains evidence linking the sale to the goods' export from Taiwan. Certain services supplied for use outside Taiwan may qualify subject to statutory conditions. A mainland China export is not a Taiwan export merely because the entity or task record refers to Taiwan; the transaction's actual supplier, place of supply, customs movement, and taxpayer registration determine treatment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Taiwan export declaration or other customs evidence showing export clearance and identifying the exported goods
Commercial invoice, sales contract, and shipping records, including bill of lading or air waybill, sufficient to link the export to the zero-rated sale
Evidence of payment and settlement retained under applicable accounting and tax-record rules; an inward remittance certificate is not a universally prescribed condition for Taiwan export zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Taiwan does not impose a general 180-day foreign-exchange repatriation deadline as a condition of export zero-rating. Unsupported or incorrectly claimed zero-rating may result in assessment of business tax, interest, administrative penalties, and recovery of improperly obtained refunds under applicable tax laws. False documents or intentional tax evasion may trigger more severe statutory sanctions. Penalties depend on the facts, applicable provisions, and any correction or disclosure procedures.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC, 中国人民银行) as the monetary authority, with the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE, 国家外汇管理局) as the exclusive administrative authority for foreign-exchange regulation, cross-border receipts and payments, BOP reporting, trade-credit monitoring, and FDI capital registration; SAFE's regulatory powers for goods-trade and capital flows are delegated to commercial banks acting as direct agents under the 'bank handling' (银行直接办理) regime, requiring every cross-border flow to be authenticated against customs and SAFE monitoring systems before execution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Renminbi is fully convertible for current-account items (goods trade, services, and investment income including dividends) subject to genuine-transaction verification, documentary evidence, and BOP declaration; capital-account items remain controlled and conditional: inbound FDI capital contributions are permitted against SAFE registration, outbound capital (equity transfer proceeds, capital reduction, liquidation distributions, external debt repayment) requires prior SAFE registration or quota approval, and all capital-account settlements follow the discretionary settlement with a negative list (no securities investment, no entrusted loans, no real-estate use outside prescribed scope). For profit remittance to a Taiwan shareholder, the legal hurdles are: (i) a PRC CPA audited statutory financial report for the fiscal year ending, (ii) a valid profit-distribution resolution of the board/shareholders, (iii) proof of 10% dividend withholding tax paid to the PRC tax authority on the gross dividend (the statutory reduced rate for non-resident passive income; the Cross-Strait Tax Cooperation Agreement, though signed, is not effectively in force in practice, so the standard 10% rate applies without a recognized treaty reduction to 5%), and (iv) execution of the remittance through the current-account investment-income BOP category with SAFE/currency-monitoring system verification; dividend remittance is not subject to capital-account licensing but banks will refuse payment where tax clearance or audit evidence is incomplete.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: China has abolished all mandatory foreign-exchange surrender and mandatory conversion ratios; the exporter may hold export receipts in its current-account FX settlement account up to the SAFE-assigned quota or settle them into RMB at the market rate at its discretion. Statutory repatriation obligations remain binding: export proceeds must be received in China, as a general rule, no later than 90 days after the customs export declaration date; where collection is later than 90 days after customs declaration, the exporter must file a deferred-receipts report (延期收款报告) in the SAFE trade-credit monitoring system within 30 days after the actual receipt; where collection is received more than 30 days before shipment, an advance-receipts report (预收货款报告) may be required for amounts exceeding the USD 50,000 equivalent threshold; banks refuse or escalate simplified settlement where the monitoring system flags overdue or unmatched receipts against customs records, and the trade-credit reporting obligation is a precondition to repeated settlement of goods-trade FX transactions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW for purely offshore digital EMI and virtual-account providers (Airwallex, Currencycloud, Wise Business, or non-PRC neobanks) used as the primary collection or disbursement rail for the WFOE; such structures bypass the SAFE goods-trade customs-verification chain, produce unverified cross-border receipts in a foreign entity account of a PRC resident exporter, trigger monitoring flags for inconsistent BOP reporting and customs-data mismatch, and expose the exporter to administrative penalties up to 30% of the unlawful foreign-exchange amount or criminal exposure for illegal FX business and evasion of verification. Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for PRC-licensed cross-border payment fintechs (e.g., LianLian Global, PingPong, XTransfer and comparable PBOC/SAFE-licensed entities) acting as a supplementary layer that provides transaction matching, trade-document digitization, and FX advisory, so long as the actual settlement leg is executed through a licensed onshore custodian commercial bank; for bulk dehydrated garlic and chili pepper export settled by LC or T/T wire, the onshore custodian bank remains the mandatory clearing counterparty and the fintech layer only accelerates reconciliation. Recommendation: do not route export proceeds to any offshore account of the WFOE or any related offshore entity; all export receipts must land in the WFOE's onshore current-account FX settlement account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Onshore Chinese banks generally mandate the physical appearance of the legal representative for the initial account-opening interview and dual-control signature execution, particularly where the beneficial owner is a Taiwan resident holding a Taiwan Compatriot Permit; however, major Tier-1 banks (Bank of China, China Merchants Bank, ICBC) now accept a hybrid protocol: the Taiwan legal representative attends a remote video interview under PBOC-sanctioned dual-video recording (双录), the mainland authorized manager or agent signs physically at the branch with a full board power of attorney and the entity seal, and a branch senior relationship manager approves after secondary due diligence. Where the Taiwan shareholder is a corporate entity, the bank requires the Taiwan parent's certificate of incorporation, shareholder register, beneficial-ownership statement for every natural person owning 25% or more, and company chop certifications, with cross-strait notarization and authentication through the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) and the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS) procedures or, where bank policy permits, certification by a PRC-registered CPA or attorney. Remote-only opening without any physical branch interaction or dual-recording is generally unavailable for first-time accounts with non-locally-present beneficial owners; a fully in-person visit by the authorized mainland manager together with the Taiwan legal representative's notarized and authenticated identity documents is the fastest and litigation-proof route, and any deviation requires prior written escalation approval from the bank's compliance department.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan corporate beneficial-owner chain: cross-strait ownership structure with a Taiwan-registered parent and natural-person shareholders holding Taiwan Compatriot Permits, triggering PEP/sanctions/high-risk-jurisdiction screening and opacity in the ownership chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Taiwan ROC business registration with company chop, current articles of incorporation and shareholder ledger, executed beneficial-ownership declaration listing every natural person with 25% or greater interest with Taiwan Compatriot Permit or passport copies, Taiwan tax-residence certificates, PRC business license with the unified social credit code, foreign-investor information reporting receipt from the MOFCOM/market-regulation system, SAFE FDI business-registration voucher, and a corporate KYC questionnaire on source of wealth and source of funds for the initial capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering (TBML) flags on bulk agricultural commodity export: dehydrated garlic flakes and crushed chili pepper are intrinsically high-volume, low-transparency physical goods with volatile commodity pricing and high potential for over- or under-invoicing and phantom shipments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete per-shipment evidentiary trail: signed purchase and sales contracts, commercial invoice, packing list, original bill of lading or air waybill with discharge port, China Customs export declaration with HS codes (0712.20 for dried vegetables/garlic, 0904.21 for dried chili), CIQ phytosanitary and food-safety inspection certificates, warehouse and cold-storage receipts, haulage and freight-forwarder invoices, marine insurance certificates, third-party price benchmarks supporting arm's-length valuation, and a traceability matrix linking each inward FX remittance to the matching customs record in the SAFE system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly established WFOE with early-stage high projected export turnover relative to stated paid-in capital, creating a thin-capitalization or shell/structuring red flag and a mismatch between actual operating substance and requested transaction volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAFE FDI business-registration voucher, SWIFT credit advices evidencing actual capital injections credited to the dedicated capital FX account, payment-instruction letters (支付命令函) showing deployment of registered capital into rent, procurement, salaries, and processing costs, CPA-issued capital verification report, 12-month rolling operating and cash-flow forecast, warehouse and processing-capacity evidence (leases, utility invoices, equipment purchase contracts), supplier and offtaker agreements, and the WFOE's first-year projected financial statements signed by the legal representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Routing and re-pricing through a Hong Kong or other offshore trading intermediate commonly used by Taiwan-based trading groups, creating a circuitous payment chain, possible round-tripping, and opacity between the PRC exporter and the ultimate end-buyer.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier demonstrating commercial substance of each leg: end-customer sales contracts with ultimate destination jurisdictions, the offshore intermediate's audited financial statements for the last two fiscal years, tax filings or tax receipts for each leg of the transaction, direct-shipping evidence from PRC port to end destination with the bill of lading naming the ultimate consignee, a written group-structuring memo justifying the offshore intermediary on credit-enhancement and concentration grounds, and an affirmative representation that no funds will return to Taiwan or any related party in Taiwan without a matching real goods or services transaction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, restricted-party, and food-regulatory screening on export counterparties and freight routes: dehydrated garlic and chili products are food commodities that attract destination-country import notifications (EU, US FDA) and could inadvertently involve sanctioned or high-risk end users or transshipment hubs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative-media and sanctions screening reports produced by the bank's own engine and independently repeated by external counsel covering all counterparties, shipping agents, banks, and ultimate consignees; end-beneficiary and ultimate-consignee attestation forms; written confirmation that the goods are exclusively for food-processing use with no dual-use or military application; certificates of lawful food-import notification in each destination country; and a pre-agreed escalation protocol under which any new buyer or financing bank is added to the verified-trade-partner whitelist before transaction execution.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol for the Taiwan investor's injection of registered capital into the PRC WFOE: (1) complete the foreign-investment information reporting with the MOFCOM/market-regulation system and obtain the unified social credit code-linked foreign-investment record; (2) execute SAFE FDI registration through the receiving bank's direct-dealing system to obtain the SAFE business-registration voucher; (3) open a dedicated foreign-currency capital FX account at the Tier-1 custodian bank, distinct from the current-account FX settlement account; (4) the Taiwan parent remits via SWIFT MT103 with remittance field specifying 'investment in registered capital' and the receiving bank performs the BOP receipts declaration under the direct-investment capital-increase code; (5) after receipt, obtain a PRC CPA capital-verification report confirming paid-in capital; (6) settle the capital into RMB under discretionary settlement with a negative list, executing a payment-instruction letter (支付命令函) for each deployment into permitted operating uses (procurement of garlic and chili raw materials, processing, rent, wages, domestic logistics), with funds prohibited from securities investment, entrusted loans, or real-estate use outside prescribed scope; (7) maintain a compliance file containing the SAFE voucher, capital-verification report, payment-instruction letters, and bank records of the negative-list compliance review; (8) report any splitting, round-tripping, or use of offshore financing routes, which is prohibited, and ensure any future increase or reduction of registered capital is pre-registered with SAFE before the corresponding remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for the export entity's outward payments: (A) domestic RMB payments to garlic/chili farmers, processors, packers, and logistics providers are settled through CNAPS/HVPS (China's high-value payment system) with no FX registration; (B) FX payments for imported raw materials and packaging (e.g., fresh garlic or dried chili sourced from India, Vietnam, or Argentina for reprocessing) are executed by SWIFT MT103 for open-account T/T or by an MT700 documentary import L/C issued by the custodian bank; the bank verifies the real goods-trade background against the customs import declaration, commercial contract, invoice, and bill of lading on a per-transaction basis, and prepayments exceeding 30% of contract value or the USD 50,000 equivalent, or with delivery intervals beyond 90 days, must be registered in the SAFE trade-credit monitoring system before payment; the BOP outward-payment declaration uses the goods-import purpose category consistent with the target payment rails (Swift_LC and TT_Wire); (C) dividend remittance to the Taiwan parent is executed by SWIFT MT103 under the current-account investment-income category after bank review of the board resolution, audited financial statements, proof of 10% dividend withholding tax payment, and tax clearance; (D) any management fee, royalty, external-debt interest, or other service remittance requires its own contract-based current-account verification or SAFE registration before execution, and all outward remittances are screened for sanctions, round-tripping, and consistency with the enterprise's registered business scope and customs data.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable FX forward contracts (远期结售汇) executed with the custodian bank against genuine and quantifiable export-receipt and import-payment exposures under SAFE's real-trade-background aggregation rules, with maturities generally capped at 12 months and no cash-settlement without actual trade flows.

FX currency swaps (外汇掉期) between the WFOE and the custodian bank to manage temporary liquidity mismatches between USD and RMB balances arising from the timing differences of export collections and import disbursements.

Vanilla RMB-versus-FX currency option combinations (risk-reversal, call/put spreads) with real trade exposure, full upfront premium settlement, and bank-policy loss-limit covenants; the options must be exercised or cash-settled only against actual FX flows and cannot be used as leveraged speculation.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) strictly limited to hedging principal and interest service of registered SAFE external debts or long-term FX liabilities, never as a standalone speculative derivative for an entity without qualifying FX liabilities.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are NOT permissible for an onshore PRC corporate as its primary hedge instrument; NDF usage is confined to the offshore interbank market and ring-fenced tail-risk structures of the PRC bank's own offshore book, so the WFOE must use deliverable forwards and vanilla options in the onshore market for all trade-related hedging.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance, Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 1 – May 31 immediately following the fiscal year-end (for December 31 fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of 1% of unpaid tax for every 2 days of delay, capped at 15%; daily interest on underpaid tax after the deadline; if never filed, tax assessed ex parte from available information plus penalty up to 3 times the assessed tax; repeated noncompliance may lead to compulsory collection and administrative strike-off of the company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and shareholders' meeting approval filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registry authority (Ministry of Economic Affairs / municipal commercial development bureaus)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end (June 30 of the following year for December 31 fiscal year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deliver prescribed statements for record within the statutory period subjects the responsible person to administrative fines of TWD 10,000; continued default after remedial notice may trigger repeated penalties and eventual revocation/strike-off of company registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (via Company Registration Information System)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 1 – March 31 of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing subject to fines of TWD 50,000 – TWD 500,000; authorities set a remedial deadline, and continued noncompliance results in repeated fines and possible registration strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent CPA audit for companies with paid-in capital exceeding NT$ 30 million, or annual revenue exceeding NT$ 100 million, or average employee headcount exceeding 100; foreign-invested enterprises and regulated financial/certain non-public companies may be required to certify financial statements regardless of threshold if so directed by competent authorities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public companies and financial institutions; Taiwan Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (TW GAAP / Enterprise Accounting Standard, EAS) for non-public companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Article 22-1 of the Taiwan Company Act, every company must file an annual registry of directors, supervisors, managers, and shareholders holding more than 10% of the shares with the Ministry of Economic Affairs during the statutory window (March 1–31). Shareholding transfers occurring before the filing window must be reflected in that annual confirmation; transfers after the filing window are captured in the next annual cycle or through an updated filing within 15 days if a new notifiable person appears.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 15,000 per year depending on transaction volume
